expanded_sentences: The patient is a 58-year-old male with a documented history of recurrent severe myocardial infarctions beginning at age 55, requiring emergency stenting and subsequent coronary artery bypass grafting.
Diabetes mellitus type 2 was diagnosed at age 48 and is currently managed with metformin, with HbA1c levels ranging between 6.5% and 7.2%.
Hypercholesterolemia was identified at age 45 with LDL levels exceeding 190 mg/dL despite lifestyle modifications.
Mild elevation of hepatic transaminases has been present since age 50, with possible etiologies including statin therapy or non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
The patient has a 20-year history of smoking (20 pack-years) but successfully quit at age 45.
Coronary artery disease was diagnosed at age 55, classified as Stage III with multivessel involvement and impaired left ventricular function.
Genetic testing confirmed a heterozygous LDLR c.1444G>A mutation, consistent with familial hypercholesterolemia.
A heart biopsy was performed during bypass surgery at age 55 years 6 months, revealing ischemic cardiomyopathy on histopathological analysis.
A peripheral blood sample was collected at age 58 for genetic analysis and lipid profile evaluation.
The patient's paternal father died at age 62 from sudden cardiac death, a relevant family history for cardiovascular risk assessment.
